note: The problem appears ancient, implicit in Euclid's work (c. 300 BC) on even perfect numbers and explicit questions about completeness. Jacques Lefèvre stated in 1496 that Euclid's rule gives all perfect numbers, implicitly denying odd perfect numbers. Euler (18th century) stated 'Whether there are any odd perfect numbers is a most difficult question' but no specific date is given. Wikipedia does not identify a definitive first posing date or originator.
